key_insight: No reconstruction method wins across all flow regimes: classical estimators remain competitive, while learned models gain an advantage as sensor density or observability decreases.
engineering_relevance: Sparse-sensor flow reconstruction should be selected for the flow regime, measured variables, uncertainty needs and computational budget rather than accuracy alone.
method: Compare 10 learned and 5 classical methods across cylinder-wake, 2D Kolmogorov and 3D isotropic flows.
Use shared leakage-controlled splits and sensor draws.
Evaluate per-channel error, ensemble spread, calibration, spectra and computational cost.
evidence_signal: Classical methods lead on the cylinder wake, inverse-distance weighting matches the best learned methods on observed 3D channels, and Kolmogorov rankings differ between pointwise error and probabilistic scoring.
watch_item: Generative ensembles remain underdispersed; larger sampler budgets improve ensemble quality at higher cost, while full-grid construction methods can exhaust memory at scale.
paper_title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
